Load behavioural model data
```{r}
behav_data_test <-read_csv(here("data", "data_WP3_model.csv")) %>%
  select(pid, trial, cond, acc, rt) %>% 
  rename(subjects = pid, S = cond, R = acc) %>% 
  mutate(subjects=factor(subjects),
         S=factor(S,
                  levels = c("Novel", "Learned")),
         R=case_when(
           R == "1" & S == "Novel" ~ "Novel",
           R == "1" & S == "Learned" ~ "Learned",
           R == "0" & S == "Novel" ~ "Learned",
           R == "0" & S == "Learned" ~ "Novel"),
         R=factor(R,
                  levels = c("Novel", "Learned"))) %>% 
  as.data.frame()

sdt_summary <- behav_data_test |>
  mutate(
    outcome = case_when(
      S == "Learned" & R == "Learned" ~ "hit",
      S == "Learned" & R == "Novel"   ~ "miss",
      S == "Novel"   & R == "Novel"   ~ "cr",
      S == "Novel"   & R == "Learned" ~ "fa"
    )
  ) |>
  count(subjects, outcome) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    hit_rate  = hit  / (hit + miss),
    miss_rate = miss / (hit + miss),
    cr_rate   = cr   / (cr + fa),
    fa_rate   = fa   / (cr + fa)
  )
```


Load pupil metrics
```{r}
mean_pid <- read_csv(here("data", "pupil_metrics", "mean_pid_trial.csv")) %>%
  select(pid, trial, condition, accuracy, mean)
max_pid <- read_csv(here("data", "pupil_metrics", "max_pid_trial.csv")) %>%
  select(pid, trial, condition, accuracy, pupil_peak_diff)
change_pid <- read_csv(here("data", "pupil_metrics", "change_pid_trial.csv")) %>%
  select(pid, trial, condition, accuracy, mean_pupil_change)



pupil_data_test <- mean_pid %>%
  mutate(max_pupil = max_pid$pupil_peak_diff,
         rate_pupil = change_pid$mean_pupil_change) %>%
  rename(S = condition,
         correct = accuracy,
         mean_pupil = mean,
         subjects = pid) %>%
  mutate(S = fct_recode(S, Novel = "unfamiliar", Learned = "learned"),
         S = factor(S, levels = c("Novel", "Learned"))) %>%
  mutate(R=case_when(
           correct == "1" & S == "Novel" ~ "Novel",
           correct == "1" & S == "Learned" ~ "Learned",
           correct == "0" & S == "Novel" ~ "Learned",
           correct == "0" & S == "Learned" ~ "Novel"),
         R=factor(R,
                  levels = c("Novel", "Learned")),
         subjects = as.factor(subjects),
         correct = case_when(
           R == "Novel" & S == "Novel" ~ "true",
           R == "Novel" & S == "Learned" ~ "false",
           R == "Learned" & S == "Novel" ~ "false",
           R == "Learned" & S == "Learned" ~ "true")
         ) %>%
  relocate(R, .before = mean_pupil) 
```


```{r}
behav_subs <- unique(as.character(behav_data_test$subjects))
pupil_subs <- unique(as.character(pupil_data_test$subjects))

only_in_behav <- setdiff(behav_subs, pupil_subs)
only_in_pupil <- setdiff(pupil_subs, behav_subs)
only_in_behav
only_in_pupil
```


Create pupil design_1
```{r}
# 1. Compare on raw character/original values, before any factor coercion
# ============================================================================
# Pupil design matrices (predictors) — built once, shared across all 3 measures
# ============================================================================
pupil_data_test$subjects <- factor(pupil_data_test$subjects, levels = levels(behav_data_test$subjects))

pupil_design_matrices <- pupil_data_test |>
  mutate(
    learned_true = as.numeric(S == "Learned" & correct == "true"),
    learned_false = as.numeric(S == "Learned" & correct == "false"),
    novel_true = as.numeric(S == "Novel" & correct == "true"),
    novel_false = as.numeric(S == "Novel" & correct == "false")
  ) |>
  group_by(subjects) |>
  group_split() |>
  setNames(levels(pupil_data_test$subjects)) |>
  map(\(d) {
    d |>
      dplyr::select(learned_true, learned_false, novel_true, novel_false) |>
      as.data.frame()
  })

# One emc.design object, reused for all three measures —
# design_fmri() only encodes the predictor structure, not the outcome column
design_pupil <- design_fmri(
  design_matrix = pupil_design_matrices,
  model = MRI
)

# ============================================================================
# Three separate outcome data sets — one "ROI-style" data frame per measure
# ============================================================================
pupil_mean_data <- pupil_data_test |>
  dplyr::select(subjects, mean_pupil) |>
  mutate(subjects = factor(subjects))

pupil_max_data <- pupil_data_test |>
  dplyr::select(subjects, max_pupil) |>
  mutate(subjects = factor(subjects))

pupil_rate_data <- pupil_data_test |>
  dplyr::select(subjects, rate_pupil) |>
  mutate(subjects = factor(subjects))

cat("=== PUPIL DESIGN (shared across mean/max/rate) ===\n")
summary(design_pupil)
```

Behavioural design
```{r}
# ============================================================================
# LBA Design: v varies by condition and accuracy, everything else fixed
# ============================================================================

matchfun <- function(d) d$S == d$lR

design_behav <- design(
  factors = list(
    subjects = levels(behav_data_test$subjects),
    S = c("Learned", "Novel")
  ),
  Rlevels = c("Learned", "Novel"),
  model = LBA,
  matchfun = matchfun,
  formula = list(
    v ~ 0 + S:lM,
    sv ~ 0 + lM,
    B ~ 0 + lR,
    A ~ 1,
    t0 ~ 1
  ),
  constants = c(sv_lMFALSE = log(1))
)

```
Joint-modelling
```{r}
#| label: fit-model

## use EMC2::make_emc() to setup an emc object for a joint model.
## note how you just list the different data and designs in order
joint_emc <- make_emc(
  data = list(
    pupil_mean = pupil_mean_data,
    behavior   = behav_data_test
  ),
  design = list(
    pupil_mean = design_pupil,
    behavior   = design_behav
  ),
  type = "standard",
  n_chains = 3,
  compress = TRUE
)

#Model 2
joint_emc_2 <- make_emc(
  data = list(
    pupil_mean = pupil_mean_data,
    behavior   = behav_data_test
  ),
  design = list(
    pupil_mean = design_pupil_2,
    behavior   = design_behav
  ),
  type = "standard",
  n_chains = 3,
  compress = TRUE
)
## fit the model_2
## this might take a while. e.g., 50 minutes on a 28 core mac studio

joint_fit <- fit(
  joint_emc_2,
  iter = 1000,
  stage = "preburn",
  step_size = 200,
  cores_for_chains = 1,
  cores_per_chain = 6,
  verbose = TRUE,
  fileName = "samples/joint_model_try_2.RData"
)

##Continue fitting
joint_fit <- fit(
  joint_fit,
  iter = 2000,
  stage = "sample",
  step_size = 200,
  cores_for_chains = 1,
  cores_per_chain = 6,
  verbose = TRUE,
  fileName = "samples/joint_model_mean.RData"
)
```

# 7. Parameter Recovery Analysis

```{r}
#| label: parameter-recovery

## ============================================================================
## 7.1 Extract posterior distributions using parameters()
## ============================================================================

# Define iteration and chain structure
iter_n <- 7689
chain_n <- 3

# Extract group-level means (mu) - behavioral and pupil parameters
mu_params <- parameters(
  joint_fit,
  selection = "mu"
) |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  mutate(
    iter = rep(1:iter_n, times = chain_n),
    chain = rep(1:chain_n, each = iter_n)
  ) |> 
  select(chain, iter, everything())

# Extract correlations
corr_params <- parameters(
  joint_fit,
  selection = "correlation"
) |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  mutate(
    iter = rep(1:iter_n, times = chain_n),
    chain = rep(1:chain_n, each = iter_n)
  ) |> 
  select(chain, iter, everything())

## ============================================================================
## 7.2 Recovery of cell means (behavioral drift rates and pupil responses)
## ============================================================================

# Convert mu parameters to long format
mu_tidy <- mu_params |>
  pivot_longer(
    -c(chain, iter),
    names_to = "parameter",
    values_to = "value"
  )

# Calculate ground truth cell means
ground_truth_means <- tibble(
  parameter = c(
    "behavior|v",
    "behavior|v_lMd",
    "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy",
    "pupil|constant",
    "pupil|condition_learned"
  ),
  true_value = c(
    mean(individual_pars$v_easy + individual_pars$v_hard) / 2,  # Grand mean drift
    1.2,                                                         # Fixed value of accuracy on drift
    mean(individual_pars$v_hard - individual_pars$v_easy),      # Condition effect
    mean(individual_pars$pupil_easy + individual_pars$pupil_hard) / 2,  # Mean pupil
    mean(individual_pars$pupil_hard - individual_pars$pupil_easy)       # Pupil condition effect
  )
)





# Define short labels for plotting
mu_short_labels <- c(
  "behavior|v" = "Drift",
  "behavior|v_lMd" = "Drift Match",
  "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy" = "Drift Δ",
  "pupil|constant" = "Pupil",
  "pupil|condition_hard" = "Pupil Δ"
)

# Prepare data for plotting
mu_plot_data <- mu_tidy |>
  filter(parameter %in% ground_truth_means$parameter) |>
  mutate(param_label = mu_short_labels[parameter])

mu_ground_truth_plot <- ground_truth_means |>
  mutate(param_label = mu_short_labels[parameter])

# Plot
ggplot(mu_plot_data, aes(x = value, y = fct_rev(param_label))) +  
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(
    fill = "#0072B2",
    alpha = 0.7,
    .width = c(0.66, 0.95)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = mu_ground_truth_plot,
    aes(x = true_value, y = fct_rev(param_label)),
    color = "#D55E00",
    size = 4,
    shape = 18
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Recovery of Group-Level Parameters",
    subtitle = "Orange diamonds show ground truth values | 66% and 95% credible intervals",
    x = "Parameter Value",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave("figures/mu_dist_recovery.jpeg",
       width = 10, height = 7)

# Numerical summary of recovery
cat("\n=== RECOVERY OF GROUP-LEVEL MEANS ===\n\n")
mu_summary <- mu_tidy |>
  filter(parameter %in% ground_truth_means$parameter) |>
  group_by(parameter) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(value),
    q025 = quantile(value, 0.025),
    q975 = quantile(value, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(ground_truth_means, by = "parameter") |>
  mutate(
    bias = median - true_value,
    coverage = true_value >= q025 & true_value <= q975,
    relative_bias = (bias / abs(true_value)) * 100,
    param_label = mu_short_labels[parameter]
  ) |>
  select(param_label, true_value, median, q025, q975, bias, relative_bias, coverage)

print(mu_summary, width = Inf)

## ============================================================================
## 7.3 Recovery of correlations
## ============================================================================

# Convert correlations to long format first (keep original parameter names)
corr_tidy <- corr_params |>
  pivot_longer(
    -c(chain, iter),
    names_to = "term",
    values_to = "value"
  )

# Calculate ground truth correlations using ORIGINAL parameter names
ground_truth_pars <- individual_pars |>
  mutate(
    `behavior|v` = (v_easy + v_hard) / 2,
    `behavior|v_conditionhard-easy` = v_hard - v_easy,
    `pupil|constant` = (pupil_easy + pupil_hard) / 2,
    `pupil|condition_hard` = pupil_hard - pupil_easy
  ) |>
  select(`behavior|v`, `behavior|v_conditionhard-easy`, `pupil|constant`, `pupil|condition_hard`)

true_corrs_key <- cor(ground_truth_pars)

# Create ground truth table for ALL 6 correlations
ground_truth_corrs <- tibble(
  term = c(
    # Cross-modal: behavior × pupil (4 correlations)
    "behavior|v.pupil|constant",
    "behavior|v.pupil|condition_hard",
    "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy.pupil|constant",
    "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy.pupil|condition_hard",
    # Within-behavior (1 correlation) - corrected name
    "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy.behavior|v",
    # Within-pupil (1 correlation)
    "pupil|constant.pupil|condition_hard"
  ),
  true_value = c(
    true_corrs_key["behavior|v", "pupil|constant"],
    true_corrs_key["behavior|v", "pupil|condition_hard"],
    true_corrs_key["behavior|v_conditionhard-easy", "pupil|constant"],
    true_corrs_key["behavior|v_conditionhard-easy", "pupil|condition_hard"],
    true_corrs_key["behavior|v", "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy"],
    true_corrs_key["pupil|constant", "pupil|condition_hard"]
  )
)

# Define SHORT names for all 6 correlations
short_labels <- c(
  "behavior|v.pupil|constant" = "Drift × Pupil",
  "behavior|v.pupil|condition_hard" = "Drift × Pupil Δ",
  "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy.pupil|constant" = "Drift Δ × Pupil",
  "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy.pupil|condition_hard" = "Drift Δ × Pupil Δ",
  "behavior|v_conditionhard-easy.behavior|v" = "Drift × Drift Δ",
  "pupil|constant.pupil|condition_hard" = "Pupil × Pupil Δ"
)

# Filter and prepare data for plotting
corr_plot_data <- corr_tidy |>
  filter(term %in% ground_truth_corrs$term) |>
  mutate(term_label = short_labels[term])

ground_truth_plot <- ground_truth_corrs |>
  mutate(term_label = short_labels[term])

# Plot all 6 correlations
ggplot(corr_plot_data, aes(x = value, y = fct_rev(term_label))) +  
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(
    fill = "#0072B2",
    alpha = 0.7,
    .width = c(0.66, 0.95)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = ground_truth_plot,
    aes(x = true_value, y = fct_rev(term_label)),
    color = "#D55E00",
    size = 4,
    shape = 18
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Recovery of All Correlations",
    subtitle = "Orange diamonds show ground truth | 66% and 95% credible intervals",
    x = "Correlation",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave("figures/corr_dist_recovery.jpeg",
       width = 10, height = 8)  # Slightly taller for 6 rows

# Numerical summary of correlation recovery
cat("\n=== RECOVERY OF ALL 6 CORRELATIONS ===\n\n")
corr_summary <- corr_tidy |>
  filter(term %in% ground_truth_corrs$term) |>
  group_by(term) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(value),
    q025 = quantile(value, 0.025),
    q975 = quantile(value, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(ground_truth_corrs, by = "term") |>
  mutate(
    bias = median - true_value,
    coverage = true_value >= q025 & true_value <= q975,
    abs_bias = abs(bias),
    term_label = short_labels[term]
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs_bias)) |>
  select(term_label, true_value, median, q025, q975, bias, coverage)

print(corr_summary, width = Inf)


## ============================================================================
## 7.4 Correlation heatmaps (key parameters only)
## ============================================================================

# Helper function to convert flat correlations to matrix
corr_vec_to_matrix <- function(corr_vec, param_names) {
  n <- length(param_names)
  mat <- matrix(1, nrow = n, ncol = n)
  rownames(mat) <- colnames(mat) <- param_names
  
  for (col_name in names(corr_vec)) {
    params <- str_split(col_name, "\\.", n = 2)[[1]]
    if (length(params) == 2) {
      i <- match(params[1], param_names)
      j <- match(params[2], param_names)
      if (!is.na(i) && !is.na(j)) {
        mat[i, j] <- mat[j, i] <- corr_vec[[col_name]]
      }
    }
  }
  mat
}

# Only the 4 key parameters that vary meaningfully
key_params <- c(
  "behavior|v",
  "behavior|v_lMTRUE:SLearned",
  "behavior|v_lMFALSE:SLearned",
  "behavior|v_lMTRUE:SNovel",
  "behavior|v_lMFALSE:SNovel",
  "pupil_mean|condition_learned",
  "pupil_mean|constant",
  "pupil_rate|condition_learned",
  "pupil_rate|constant"
)

short_names_key <- c(
  "behavior|v" = "Drift",
  "behavior|v_lMTRUE:SLearned" = "Drift_learned_true",
  "behavior|v_lMFALSE:SLearned" = "Drift_learned_false" ,
  "behavior|v_lMTRUE:SNovel" = "Drift_novel_true",
  "behavior|v_lMFALSE:SNovel" = "Drift_novel_false",
  "pupil_mean|constant" = "Pupil_mean",
  "pupil_mean|condition_learned" = "Pupil mean Δ",
  "pupil_rate|constant" = "Pupil rate",
  "pupil_rate|condition_learned" = "Pupil rate Δ"
)

# Calculate estimated correlation matrix (posterior medians) - 4x4
median_corrs <- corr_params |>
  select(-chain, -iter) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), median))

est_corr_matrix <- corr_vec_to_matrix(median_corrs, key_params)
rownames(est_corr_matrix) <- colnames(est_corr_matrix) <- short_names_key[key_params]

# Calculate ground truth correlation matrix - 4x4
ground_truth_varying <- individual_pars |>
  mutate(
    `behavior|v` = (v_easy + v_hard) / 2,
    `behavior|v_conditionhard-easy` = v_hard - v_easy,
    `pupil|constant` = (pupil_easy + pupil_hard) / 2,
    `pupil|condition_hard` = pupil_hard - pupil_easy
  ) |>
  select(all_of(key_params))

true_corr_matrix <- cor(ground_truth_varying)
rownames(true_corr_matrix) <- colnames(true_corr_matrix) <- short_names_key[key_params]

# Calculate difference
diff_corr_matrix <- est_corr_matrix - true_corr_matrix

# Create plots (upper triangle only)
p_true <- ggcorrplot::ggcorrplot(
  true_corr_matrix,
  method = "square",
  type = "upper",
  lab = TRUE,
  lab_size = 3,
  title = "Ground Truth",
  legend.title = "Correlation"
)
p_true

p_estimated <- ggcorrplot::ggcorrplot(
  est_corr_matrix,
  method = "square",
  type = "upper",
  lab = TRUE,
  lab_size = 3,
  title = "Estimated",
  legend.title = "Correlation"
)
p_estimated

ggsave("figures/corr_matrix_joint.jpeg", width = 18, height = 10, dpi = 800) 

p_diff <- ggcorrplot::ggcorrplot(
  diff_corr_matrix,
  method = "square",
  type = "upper",
  lab = TRUE,
  lab_size = 3,
  title = "Error (Est − True)",
  legend.title = "Correlation"
)
p_diff

# Combine plots
(p_true | p_estimated | p_diff) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Correlation Matrix Recovery (Key Parameters)",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
  )

ggsave("figures/corr_mat_recovery.jpeg",
       width = 10, height = 7)

    q025 = quantile(value, 0.025),
    q975 = quantile(value, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(ground_truth_corrs, by = "term") |>
  mutate(
    bias = median - true_value,
    coverage = true_value >= q025 & true_value <= q975
  )

print(corr_summary, width = Inf)

cat("\n\nCOVERAGE RATES:\n")
cat("Parameters:", mean(mu_summary$coverage) * 100, "% coverage\n")
cat("Correlations:", mean(corr_summary$coverage) * 100, "% coverage\n")

cat("\n\nMEAN ABSOLUTE BIAS:\n")
cat("Parameters:", mean(abs(mu_summary$bias)), "\n")
cat("Correlations:", mean(abs(corr_summary$bias)), "\n")
```
